s1.syndrome_frame: Acute monocular vision loss with associated orbital and adnexal inflammation
salient_findings: Pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of the eyelids and forearm
Tense eyelid edema, chemosis, and corneal haze
Serous retinal detachment and macular whitening
key_facts: Obese man in his mid-30s
No prior systemic or ocular disorders
Heavy alcohol consumption the night prior
Took 2 buprenorphine hydrochloride/naloxone hydrochloride pills
Denies any trauma
Visual acuity: No light perception in right eye, 20/20 in left eye
Intraocular pressure: 37 mm Hg in right eye, 21 mm Hg in left eye
Creatinine level: 2.2 mg/dL
Creatine kinase level: 29,320 U/L
Periorbital soft-tissue swelling on noncontrast computed tomography
Severe disorganization of retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography
Delayed choroidal filling and poor vascular perfusion on Fluorescein Angiography

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden vision loss in one eye with evidence of retinal ischemia on imaging

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute monocular vision loss with associated orbital and adnexal inflammation, elevated creatinine and creatine kinase levels

shortlist.label: Ischemic Optic Neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden vision loss in one eye with optic disc swelling and retinal ischemia on imaging

shortlist.label: Purtscher-like Retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Trauma-like retinopathy with vision loss, retinal whitening, and poor vascular perfusion on imaging, possibly related to buprenorphine/naloxone intake

shortlist.label: Susac Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute vision loss with retinal vasculitis, possible microemboli, and poor vascular perfusion on imaging

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with sudden vision loss, periorbital edema, and retinal findings such as serous retinal detachment and severe disorganization of retinal architecture, combined with the recent history of heavy alcohol consumption and buprenorphine/naloxone use, is most consistent with Purtscher-like Retinopathy, which is known to be associated with various forms of trauma, including drug and alcohol use.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: While CRAO could explain the sudden vision loss and retinal findings, it typically does not present with periorbital edema or such significant systemic symptoms as elevated creatine kinase levels.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
rejected.why: GCA is unlikely given the patient's age and lack of prior systemic symptoms such as headache, jaw claudication, or polymyalgia rheumatica.

rejected.label: Ischemic Optic Neuropathy
rejected.why: ION could explain the vision loss but does not typically present with the retinal and periorbital findings seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Susac Syndrome
rejected.why: Susac Syndrome is a rare condition characterized by retinal vasculopathy, encephalopathy, and hearing loss, which does not match the patient's presentation focused on vision loss and periorbital findings without mention of neurological or auditory symptoms.

gold: Saturday night retinopathy with orbital compression syndrome
